Definition: accusative case of a derivative of the base of G3145 (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose:--in vain.
BiblicalUsage: In vain means to no purpose, and Jesus uses it once in each Gospel for the same charge: the Pharisees worship God in vain, teaching the commandments of men as doctrine. Their worship looks right, but it is empty because it honours tradition over God's word.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that worship is only real when it follows what God actually said, and any rule we add to His word turns the whole thing vain.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
